decisions.summary: the one parse of every other class not built
decisions.why: Not one of the GM's named items (the named item, the page from the map's records, is the 83% A2 built); it served only the general clause, whose criterion is 'significantly faster'. R2 puts every other class at about 17% of 1.597 s (about 0.27 s over two maps, all four parses together), so a single parse saves less than that. But the plan's and spec's stated '0.09 s (research R2)' is not in R2 or measurements.json and must be corrected or keyed.

A GM-named lever dropped, but on a measurement taken in the configuration that ships (base fit search, FR-014, the connector fix; astarcmp at 2727c1e4b): 26 first-roll strandings against 5, four re-rolls against two, 192.9 s against 198.7 s. The GM's permission is conditioned on speed ('if those changes would allow it to be significantly faster', 'I even prefer it if it gets us performance benefits'); a lever that buys none and strands houses defeats that purpose.

decisions.summary: the coarser lattice withdrawn: 12 px strands houses the 10 px lattice did not
decisions.why: A GM-named lever ('on a coarser grid') dropped on a measurement of a router that does not ship. b2/results.json was committed at 05b13c871, when lattice_search was A* and the B3 lever was active and the connector defect unfixed; the amendment says so ('Measured with A* in the router at every cell'). R6 then shows the router itself decides which maps strand (Sawada 15 of 19 under A*, none in cost order) and R4 says strandings move chaotically with the cell, so an A*-controlled comparison says nothing about the cell under Dijkstra. R4's row '10 (the base)' is not the base (8 unreached; the cost-order base has 5 per R6). FR-003's rule is about the cell the shipped router runs on. Re-run b2/harness.py on the clone as it now stands (Dijkstra, base fit, FR-014, the connector fix), with the rescue-rounds scenario and the toys plan B2 names, and withdraw or take by that.

decisions.summary: the field search without its blind probe withdrawn: the moved maps re-roll more, slower in all
decisions.why: A GM-named lever ('the paddy field's size found from a better first guess') dropped on a measurement taken with A* in the router: b3cmp ran at 08761a0dd (20:01), where lattice_search was still A*, withdrawn three minutes later (2727c1e4b) because it strands houses. The lever's own stage saving is measured and real (1.51 -> 1.06 s Inashiro, 2.89 -> 2.21 s Sawada); the withdrawal rests entirely on six re-rolls against four, and re-rolls are exactly what A* was shown to inflate (A* with the base search re-rolled 4, cost order 2). Kashikawa was checked under both routers, the other maps and the totals were not. Re-run b3cmp/harness.py on the shipped router before withdrawing.

decisions.summary: rows as arrays withdrawn: the edge walk 3.6x slower in arrays
decisions.why: FR-005's own keep-if-faster rule. The measurement is per call (the same 3,310 verdicts, 0.312 s against 0.086 s), so it holds whatever the number of carves (R5's 'after B3' share is stale now B3 is withdrawn, but more carves only means more of the loss). The unbuilt pushes' whole scalar cost (0.024 s) is below the loss already measured.
